title: "Sovereign models are an architectural choice"
description: "Sovereignty is not a property supplied by downloading model weights."
date: 2026-02-03
categories: [Sovereign AI, Small models, Architecture]
image: cover.svg

It is tempting to treat a locally hosted model as a sovereign model. Local inference matters, but sovereignty concerns control across the whole system: models, data, infrastructure, dependencies and operating knowledge.

## Think in dependencies

A useful assessment begins with a dependency map rather than a model leaderboard.

| Layer | Questions |
|---|---|
| Model | Can the weights and licence support the intended use? |
| Data | Where do training, retrieval and evaluation data reside? |
| Runtime | Which proprietary services, drivers or accelerators are required? |
| Operations | Can the system be monitored, repaired and upgraded locally? |
| Governance | Who can inspect its evidence, decisions and changes? |

A system may be locally deployed while remaining operationally dependent on opaque components. Conversely, a carefully governed hosted component might be compatible with an organisation's actual sovereignty requirements.

## Sovereignty is contextual

There is no single threshold at which a system becomes sovereign. The relevant degree of control depends on the risk, jurisdiction, continuity requirements and sensitivity of the task.

::: {.callout-tip title="A more useful design question"}
Ask which dependencies must remain under whose control—and what happens when each external dependency disappears.
:::

This turns sovereignty from a slogan into a set of testable architectural requirements.
